title: The Iron Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1871, in a river city still smoldering from a civil war nobody won cleanly, Edmund Thornbury is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock—a job that should take two weeks and attract no attention. But the new census taker, cataloguing survivors for the victors' official history, keeps asking why Edmund's name appears on no regimental roll, no parish record, no debt ledger. Edmund's secret—that they were born Edmund Thornbury of the Iron Regiment's founding family and have spent seven years passing as an unremarkable apprentice—begins to unravel as the census taker closes in. Racing to get their true testimony notarized before the river ice breaks and the historians' version hardens into law, Edmund must choose between erasure and exposure, and discovers that belonging cannot be inherited or hidden—only claimed.
about_author: I. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing census fragments and regimental ledgers from border cities. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Establishes their careful, invisible life as an apprentice clockmaker: precise hands, rented room, no past discussed. The summons to the observatory arrives with a seal Edmund recognizes from childhood—their family crest. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Summons in Winter
chapters.summary: Edmund travels through the frozen city to the observatory, noting war damage and new victors' banners. They accept the commission despite the crest, telling themselves names mean nothing now. Emotional beat: rationalization straining against instinct.

chapters.title: The Master Clock's Heart
chapters.summary: Edmund inspects the great clock, finding sabotage—not wear—in the escapement. Someone wanted time itself stopped at the hour the city fell. POV shifts briefly to the observatory keeper, Marta, who watches this stranger too closely. Emotional beat: unease.

chapters.title: The Census Taker Arrives
chapters.summary: Census taker Adeline Voss appears at the observatory with her ledger, brisk and courteous, counting survivors for the Commission on Reconciliation. She asks Edmund standard questions; Edmund gives rehearsed answers. One answer doesn't match her notes. Emotional beat: first crack.

chapters.title: Questions in the Gallery
chapters.summary: Adeline returns with follow-ups over tea Marta provides. Why does an apprentice know the observatory's original floor plan? Edmund deflects with technical talk about gear trains. POV alternates; Adeline privately flags the file. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse politeness.

chapters.title: What the Clock Remembers
chapters.summary: Repairing the chime mechanism, Edmund finds a brass plate engraved by their father—proof the Thornburys built this clock. They pocket it. Flashback: the family's fall when the Regiment was declared traitorous. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Edmund visits the records hall under pretext, searching for their own name. A clerk mentions the Commission is compiling a definitive register; anything unwritten by spring thaw becomes 'unverifiable.' Emotional beat: the stakes sharpen—time limit established.

chapters.title: Marta's Watch
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. She recognizes something in Edmund's hands—the way they wind a key like old Aldous Thornbury did. She says nothing but leaves the archive key on the workbench. Emotional beat: unexpected, dangerous kindness.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Edmund breaks into the observatory archive at night, finds the Regiment's founding charter bearing their signature as a child witness. Footsteps above—they hide among the clockworks as Adeline works late below. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration.

chapters.title: An Honest Lie
chapters.summary: Adeline confronts Edmund gently: your papers say you arrived in 1864, yet you knew the pre-war bell schedule. Edmund offers a half-truth—an apprenticeship under a dead master. Adeline accepts it visibly, doubts invisibly. Emotional beat: guilt of survival.

chapters.title: The Old Comrade
chapters.summary: In a tavern, Edmund spots Sergeant Brann, once their father's man, now destitute and drinking. Brann recognizes them instantly—and demands money for silence. Edmund pays. Emotional beat: the past has teeth and a price.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Atmospheric interlude, Edmund's POV. The thaw timeline: six weeks until the ice breaks, when the Commission seals its register and barges carry the histories downstream. Edmund calculates what testimony requires: a notary, two witnesses, courage. Emotional beat: resolve forming.

chapters.title: What Brann Knows
chapters.summary: Brann's POV. He remembers the night the Regiment fell—remembers a child smuggled out through the clock tower tunnels. He wonders if blackmail is betrayal or wages owed. He drinks and decides it's both. Emotional beat: complicity examined.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Trace
chapters.summary: Edmund traces the clock's sabotage to a filed gear stamped with a Commission workshop mark. The victors froze the clock deliberately—to control the official hour of surrender. Emotional beat: outrage; the history is being manufactured.

chapters.title: Adeline's Own File
chapters.summary: Adeline's POV. We learn she lost brothers in the war and took the census job believing accurate memory honors the dead. Her supervisor instructs her to close 'inconvenient' entries. She hesitates over Edmund's file. Emotional beat: her faith cracking.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Edmund offers Marta the truth in exchange for her testimony. Marta reveals she kept the observatory running through the occupation precisely so someone would come back to fix it—she was waiting for a Thornbury. Emotional beat: belonging offered, cautiously accepted.

chapters.title: Brann Talks
chapters.summary: Brann, drunk, tells a Commission clerk about the Thornbury child. The clerk writes it down—but files it under rumor, since the register prefers tidy narratives. Edmund learns of the leak secondhand. Emotional beat: hunted feeling; the net tightens.

chapters.title: The Notary Problem
chapters.summary: Every notary in the city answers to the Commission. Edmund's only option: a disgraced notary, Okafor, struck off for certifying traitor wills, living above a chandler's shop. Emotional beat: allies are found among the fallen.

chapters.title: Okafor's Price
chapters.summary: Okafor agrees to certify Edmund's deposition—for a fee Edmund can't pay, unless they sell their father's tools. The tools are the last thing of the old life. Edmund begins polishing them for sale. Emotional beat: sacrifice made tangible.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tea
chapters.summary: Adeline invites Edmund to her rooms, ostensibly for form-filling. She lays out discrepancies like cards. Edmund, cornered, tells her a larger truth without the name: 'Some people survived by becoming no one.' Something shifts in her face. Emotional beat: intimacy through confession-adjacent honesty.

chapters.title: The Tools Go
chapters.summary: Edmund sells the tools to a pawnbroker who sneers at their quality. Walking home lighter-handed and heavier-hearted, they pass the ruined Regiment barracks. A child asks what it was. Edmund says: 'Home, once.' Emotional beat: mourning the self they built.

chapters.title: Marta's Testimony
chapters.summary: Marta gives her sworn statement to Okafor: she attests Edmund Thornbury maintained the master clock and its maker's legacy through seven years of silence. First page of the deposition complete. Emotional beat: momentum, fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Commission Closes In
chapters.summary: Adeline's supervisor, reading Brann's rumor file, orders Edmund detained for questioning after the register seals—after the ice breaks. Adeline sees the order. She has days, not weeks, to decide whose side accuracy falls on. Emotional beat: ticking clock made literal.

chapters.title: What Edmund Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Edmund's POV: the night of the fall, age fourteen, father pressing the brass plate and a false name into their hands, saying 'Be small. Be useful. Live.' The origin of the invisibility strategy—and its cost. Emotional beat: understanding one's own wounds.

chapters.title: Adeline Makes Copies
chapters.summary: Adeline secretly duplicates Edmund's file and the sabotage evidence, unsure why. Her POV: she tells herself it's archival diligence. It's also conscience. Emotional beat: quiet defection beginning.

chapters.title: Sabotage Discovered
chapters.summary: Commission engineers inspect the repaired clock and find the filed gear replaced—with the original stamped part preserved as evidence. Someone is building a case against the Commission. Suspicion falls on the observatory staff. Emotional beat: danger at the door.

chapters.title: Marta Detained
chapters.summary: Guards take Marta for questioning about the archive break-in. Edmund watches from the crowd, unseen, unable to help without exposing everything. Guilt compounds. Emotional beat: the price of invisibility—watching friends pay for you.

chapters.title: Brann's Choice
chapters.summary: Brann, sobered by what his gossip caused, comes to Edmund—not for money, but offering to testify about the Regiment's final night, including who ordered the clock stopped. Redemption sought, grudgingly accepted. Emotional beat: unlikely alliance.

chapters.title: The Deposition
chapters.summary: In Okafor's back room by lamplight, Edmund speaks their full name and history onto the record: birth, the fall, the escape, the years as no one. Okafor certifies each page. Emotional beat: catharsis—the self restored in ink.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Chandler's
chapters.summary: Commission agents raid Okafor's lodging, tipped by the clerk who took Brann's first story. The deposition pages survive only because Adeline had copied them. Okafor is taken. Emotional beat: despair; the record itself seized.

chapters.title: Adeline Crosses
chapters.summary: Adeline delivers the surviving copies to Edmund and confesses her role, her losses, her choice: 'I count the living. You're alive. That's my whole mandate.' She commits to testifying. Emotional beat: trust forged in treason.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Under the Tower
chapters.summary: Edmund leads Adeline and Brann through the childhood escape route beneath the observatory to retrieve the original charter and brass plate—physical proof predating the Commission. Emotional beat: returning to the wound and walking out changed.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Groan
chapters.summary: The river cracks audibly; thaw is days away. The register seals at the ice-break ceremony, where officials will read the official history aloud. Edmund plans to interrupt the reading with the true record. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Marta Returns
chapters.summary: Marta is released—her questioning produced nothing provable—and joins the plan, insisting the reading happen at the observatory steps, within earshot of the master clock she'll set striking the true hour. Emotional beat: the found family assembled.

chapters.title: Eve of the Reading
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: Edmund cleans the clock one last time, oils every gear, winds it fully. Each character prepares in their own way—Adeline copies documents, Brann sobers, Okafor waits in custody hoping. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Climax begins. At the ceremony, the official history is read as the river shatters behind the speakers. Edmund steps forward, name spoken aloud for the first time in seven years, and presents the certified deposition. Guards move. Emotional beat: terror and triumph entwined.

chapters.title: The Master Clock Speaks
chapters.summary: As chaos erupts, Marta releases the escapement; the long-stopped clock strikes the true hour across the square, drowning the officials' voices. The crowd—survivors all—hears both the bells and Edmund's testimony. Adeline reads the record publicly. Emotional beat: the city's memory reclaimed.

chapters.title: After the Flood
chapters.summary: Fallout: the register is reopened pending review; the sabotage inquiry implicates the Commission workshop; Okafor is reinstated; Brann's testimony earns him a pension, not a pardon, which he calls fair. Edmund faces neither prison nor glory—just scrutiny. Emotional beat: imperfect justice accepted.

chapters.title: A Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Resolution. Spring. Edmund repaints the observatory workshop sign: 'Thornbury & Keeper, Clockmakers.' Adeline brings the amended census page for Edmund to verify—name, trade, history, all on the record. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Hour Keeps
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Edmund's POV. The master clock runs true; Edmund teaches two apprentices, one of them the child from the barracks street. Closing meditation: survival was the price, the record was the inheritance, and the keeping of time—honest time—is the belonging. Final image: the pendulum swinging steady over the thawing river. Emotional beat: peace earned.
